groups.title: STARTTLS accepted but TLS handshake never followed
groups.why_it_matters: The client asked to upgrade to TLS and the server agreed, but no handshake followed. This is the signature of STARTTLS stripping or a broken client. Anything sent next may be readable in transit.

groups.title: Forward secrecy not used (RSA key exchange chosen by server)
groups.why_it_matters: With RSA key exchange, recording today's traffic and stealing the server key later decrypts past sessions (harvest now, decrypt later).

groups.title: STARTTLS is opportunistic on server-to-server port 25
groups.why_it_matters: Port 25 between mail servers normally uses opportunistic TLS, so a downgrade would go unnoticed. Common and often accepted, listed for awareness.

b-f01.title: STARTTLS accepted but TLS handshake never followed
b-f01.why_it_matters: The client asked to upgrade to TLS and the server agreed, but no handshake followed. This is the signature of STARTTLS stripping or a broken client. Anything sent next may be readable in transit.
b-f01.observed: STARTTLS command sent, '220 2.0.0 Ready to start TLS' returned, no ClientHello observed before the connection closed.

reason_codes.explanation: Server signalled ready but no ClientHello followed.
Same client IPs completed TLS on other servers or earlier captures.
Submission service relies on STARTTLS without enforcing encryption.

b-f01.recommendation: Enforce encryption on the submission service and re-capture to verify.

b-f02.title: Forward secrecy not used (RSA key exchange chosen by server)
b-f02.why_it_matters: With RSA key exchange, recording today's traffic and stealing the server key later decrypts past sessions (harvest now, decrypt later).
b-f02.observed: Client offered ECDHE suites; server selected TLS 1.2 AES256-SHA256 with RSA key exchange.

reason_codes.explanation: Non-AEAD cipher chosen although AEAD suites were offered.
Captured traffic stays decryptable if the key leaks.

b-f02.recommendation: Restrict Dovecot to TLS 1.2+ with ECDHE AEAD suites and re-capture to verify.

b-f03.title: STARTTLS is opportunistic on server-to-server port 25
b-f03.why_it_matters: Port 25 between mail servers normally uses opportunistic TLS, so a downgrade would go unnoticed. Common and often accepted, listed for awareness.
b-f03.observed: Server advertises STARTTLS on port 25; all observed peer sessions upgraded, enforcement not visible in a passive capture.
b-f03.recommendation: No configuration change recommended; consider MTA-STS or DANE if policy requires enforced TLS.
